Although its Git history does not line up directly with the metadata vulnerable/fixed commits, the staged tree still contains the vulnerable raw `CBS_data(cbs)` call at `fuzz/ssl_ctx_api.cc:482` and matches the saved ASan line numbers in `ssl/ssl_privkey.cc`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42541538 (boringssl): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target ssl_ctx_api [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42541538
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced the crash with the exact 1-byte witness `0x2d`. `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` initializes a `CBS` over that byte, `CBS_get_u8()` consumes it into `index == 45`, and the underlying `cbs_get()` logic advances the cursor so the remaining slice has `len == 0` and `data == buf + 1`. Selector 45 reaches the final `kAPIs` lambda, which calls `SSL_CTX_set1_sigalgs_list(ctx, (const char *)CBS_data(cbs))` directly. That passes the empty remainder's end pointer as a textual `const char *` even though `SSL_CTX_set1_sigalgs_list()` expects a NUL-terminated signature-algorithm list. In `parse_sigalgs_list()`, the initial loop `for (const char *p = str; *p; p++)` counts characters until `\0`, but here `str` already equals the first byte past the 1-byte fuzz allocation, so evaluating `*p` is immediately out of bounds. AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `ssl/ssl_privkey.cc:614`. The fix only changes the fuzz target: it first extracts a `std::string` with `GetString()` and then passes `sigalgs.c_str()`, restoring the required NUL termination.

source.description: Source. First non-harness project statement that consumes the attacker-derived `str` as a textual signature-algorithm list.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly one byte `0x2d` (`'-'`). `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` consumes that byte into `index == 45`, leaving `CBS_len(cbs) == 0`; the selected final `kAPIs` lambda then passes `CBS_data(cbs)` as `str`, so at this source step `str` already equals the one-past-end address of the 1-byte fuzzer allocation.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The loop's first `*p` read expects a NUL-terminated string and instead dereferences the one-past-end pointer passed from the harness.
sink.note: The saved ASan stack is `parse_sigalgs_list -> SSL_CTX_set1_sigalgs_list -> std::function::operator() -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`, matching this sink.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The fuzz target passes the remaining `CBS` bytes directly as a `const char *` without materializing a NUL-terminated string first.
root_cause.note: For the exact 1-byte witness, `CBS_get_u8` has already consumed the only byte, so `CBS_len(cbs) == 0` and `CBS_data(cbs)` equals the end of the 1-byte allocation. The fix replaces this call with `GetString(&sigalgs, cbs)` and `sigalgs.c_str()`.

tainted_value_origin.description: Immediate origin of the end pointer later passed as `str`. On the 1-byte witness, `CBS_get_u8` consumes `0x2d` into `index` and leaves the `CBS` cursor empty, so subsequent `CBS_data(cbs)` points one byte past the allocation.

parser_admitted.description: The exact witness byte is `0x2d`, so this dispatch selects entry 45, the final `kAPIs` lambda at lines 481-482 that calls `SSL_CTX_set1_sigalgs_list`.

fine_trace.note: On the exact 1-byte witness, `CBS_get_u8()` succeeds once, stores `index == 45`, and, via `cbs_get()`, advances `cbs->data` by one byte while decrementing `cbs->len` to zero. After this step the remaining `CBS` slice is empty and `CBS_data(cbs)` equals the one-past-end address of the 1-byte fuzz buffer.

Because step 1 produced `index == 45`, the `kAPIs[index % OPENSSL_ARRAY_SIZE(kAPIs)]` dispatch reaches this lambda. It forwards `CBS_data(cbs)` directly as a textual C string without `GetString()` or any other NUL-terminating copy. With `CBS_len(cbs) == 0`, that argument is already the one-past-end pointer of the 1-byte fuzz buffer.

Source. This is the first non-harness project statement that consumes the attacker-derived pointer as a signature-algorithm string. `SSL_CTX_set1_sigalgs_list()` has no length parameter, so it interprets `str` as a NUL-terminated textual specification and hands it to `parse_sigalgs_list()`.

Sink. The parser immediately evaluates `*p` to start counting the textual list length and `:` separators. Because steps 2 and 3 passed a one-past-end pointer instead of a NUL-terminated string, this first read is the saved AddressSanitizer `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `ssl/ssl_privkey.cc:614`.

format.contract: Exact 1-byte input `0x2d` (`'-'`). In the staged harness, that byte is consumed as `index == 45`, selecting the `SSL_CTX_set1_sigalgs_list` lambda. No bytes remain in `cbs`, so the call passes `CBS_data(cbs)` (the one-past-end pointer of the 1-byte buffer) as `str`, and `parse_sigalgs_list` immediately overreads it while scanning for `\0`.
